name: on the wire: every accepted request is answered with a stream, whatever the server chose, on the 1:1 route

only.reason: It asserts on the HTTP reply itself (status, content type, headers and SSE frames), which only a bare HTTP client sees; an SDK hands its caller the decoded result.

name: on the wire: every accepted request is answered with a stream, on the mux

only.reason: It asserts on the HTTP reply itself (status, content type, headers and SSE frames), which only a bare HTTP client sees; an SDK hands its caller the decoded result.

name: on the wire: plain HTTP statuses are only for requests refused before a stream opens

only.reason: It asserts on the HTTP reply itself (status, content type, headers and SSE frames), which only a bare HTTP client sees; an SDK hands its caller the decoded result.

name: on the wire: progress frames carry the client's token, and the server only ever sees the gateway's

only.reason: It reads the progress token on each SSE frame and the token the server was handed; an SDK shows its caller progress events without their token.

name: on the wire: a slow reply is preceded by comment lines that keep the stream alive

only.reason: It counts the SSE comment lines before the result; every SDK discards comment lines before its caller sees anything.

name: on the wire: log messages and unknown notifications never reach the client's stream

only.reason: It checks that nothing but the result is written to the stream; an SDK would drop an unknown notification itself, so its caller cannot tell whether the gateway did.

name: on the wire: a lost reply is progress, then one JSON-RPC error, then the end of the stream

only.reason: It asserts on the HTTP reply itself (status, content type, headers and SSE frames), which only a bare HTTP client sees; an SDK hands its caller the decoded result.

name: on the wire: a server's failure after the stream opened is an error inside a 200 stream

only.reason: It asserts on the HTTP reply itself (status, content type, headers and SSE frames), which only a bare HTTP client sees; an SDK hands its caller the decoded result.

name: on the wire: whatever a server sends back, the client gets one final message and the gateway keeps serving

only.reason: It feeds the gateway malformed server replies and checks only that one final message comes back on a 200 stream; what each SDK then makes of a malformed result is that SDK's own behaviour, not the gateway's.

name: on the wire: malformed client requests each get one answer, and the gateway keeps serving

only.reason: It sends request bodies no typed SDK call can produce (params that are not objects, names that are not strings, an id that is an object).

name: wire progress order: progress frames precede the result on the request's own SSE stream, under the client's token

only.reason: It reads the SSE frames themselves, their order and the progress token on each; an SDK hands its caller the events and the result, not the frames.

name: on the wire: every kind of result the gateway writes carries resultType, on the 1:1 route

only.reason: It reads resultType on the result exactly as the gateway wrote it. The TypeScript SDK removes that field before its caller sees the result, and the Go SDK fills it in, so only the wire shows what was sent.

name: on the wire: every kind of result the gateway writes carries resultType, on the mux

only.reason: It reads resultType on the result exactly as the gateway wrote it. The TypeScript SDK removes that field before its caller sees the result, and the Go SDK fills it in, so only the wire shows what was sent.

name: on the wire: every kind of result the gateway writes carries resultType, in search mode

only.reason: It reads resultType on the result exactly as the gateway wrote it. The TypeScript SDK removes that field before its caller sees the result, and the Go SDK fills it in, so only the wire shows what was sent.
